eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service model guidance and ensemble runs indicate a persistent marine layer and onshore flow will limit afternoon heating across the Los Angeles basin on May 29, keeping official high temperatures clustered in the upper 60s. This pattern aligns with typical late-May climatology when the subtropical ridge weakens and allows cool, moist air from the Pacific to moderate coastal maxima, well below the May average of 73–75 °F. Light winds and possible morning low clouds further suppress peak readings, producing the tight market clustering around the 66–69 °F bins. Updated short-range forecasts and next NWS briefing will provide the final resolution inputs.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from PAGASA place Manila’s daily high near 35°C on May 29, aligning with the month’s climatological peak when average maxima reach 33–34°C amid the transition to the southwest monsoon. Recent model runs and surface observations indicate partly cloudy conditions with isolated afternoon thunderstorms that typically cap peak heating, supporting the 43% market-implied probability for 35°C and 26% for 36°C. No significant tropical cyclone activity or anomalous heat advection has emerged in the past week to alter this outlook. Updated PAGASA guidance and ensemble model runs over the next 48 hours will refine the exact maximum before resolution.
